facts.text: Pearblossom got its name from the many pear farms that bloomed on the southern ridge of Antelope Valley.
The town sits in the Mojave Desert’s Antelope Valley and was first settled by Kitanemuk and Serrano tribes before European-American homesteaders arrived in the mid‑1800s.
Pearblossom’s quiet agricultural roots are still visible in the abandoned farms that have returned to desert or been replaced by small‑scale housing.
The town’s main street, Route 138, is notorious for being one of the most dangerous roads in the U.S., a fact that locals joke about while driving.
Pearblossom was the setting for the 1993 film “Body Bags” segment “The Gas Station,” showing the town’s quirky place in Hollywood history.
In the 1939 novel Ask the Dust, Pearblossom is mentioned in the movie adaptation starring Colin Farrell and Salma Hayek, linking the town to a classic literary work.
